name: pixelate-region
title: Pixelate Region
description: Covers chosen rectangles of a scene with an opaque mosaic and leaves the rest perfectly sharp, the way a demo hides keys, tokens and addresses. Runs its WebGL shader over its own built-in scene (a credentials page; title, rows and note from variables, with the values of the chosen rows covered), not over the host video.
useWhen: A product demo shows real data (API keys, tokens, email addresses, account numbers) that must not leave the building.
The reveal is the point: something is deliberately hidden and the viewer should see that it was hidden.
avoidWhen: The whole frame wants a treatment rather than a covered rectangle: vhs-filter and crt-screen work edge to edge.
What you are covering moves around the frame: a region is a fixed rectangle.
You only want to de-emphasise something: a mosaic dense enough to redact is not a soft focus.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Title
variables.description: Heading of the sample settings page.

variables.label: Rows
variables.description: Rows as label | value, separated by semicolons (up to 5).
variables.default: Account | casey@example.com; API key | sk_live_4f8a2c9e1b7d; Webhook secret | whsec_71c0d4e8ab35

variables.label: Note
variables.default: Rotate keys from the dashboard — old ones stay valid for 24 hours.

variables.label: Covered rows
variables.description: Numbers of the rows whose value is covered, separated by commas.

variables.label: Cell size
variables.description: Size of one mosaic cell. Pixel sizes are for a 1280×720 frame and scale with the frame.

variables.label: Resolution
variables.description: Share of the frame size the shader is drawn at, then scaled up. Mosaic cells are large; 0.75 keeps the sharp text around them crisp.
